note: Ground-truth labels for pipeline evaluation. Each entry is a flagged alert and the verdict a human analyst would reach, with the specific signals that drove it. Running `npm run eval` submits each alert through POST /api/alerts and compares the model's recommended_action to expected_action.

scoring_rules.close: both are in the escalation group {ESCALATE_SAR, CONFIRM_FRAUD, MANUAL_REVIEW} or both in {CLEAR_FALSE_POSITIVE}

cases.narrative: High-value wire to an offshore holding entity in a high-risk geography, first occurrence in this account's 12-month history.
cases.rationale: First-time offshore wire + high-risk geography is a classic SAR trigger.

cases.narrative: Three transfers just under the $10,000 reporting threshold within 48 hours, consistent with structuring to evade CTR filing.
cases.rationale: Structuring is a per-se SAR-reportable BSA violation.

cases.narrative: Account received 14 inbound transfers from 9 different senders totalling $82,000 over 3 days, then forwarded the full balance to a single beneficiary within hours — classic money mule behavior.
cases.rationale: Fan-in/fan-out with rapid pass-through is the textbook mule pattern.

cases.narrative: Login from unrecognized device in a foreign country followed immediately by a $47,000 outbound wire. Customer has never transacted internationally before.
cases.rationale: Device + geo anomaly immediately before a large outbound wire with no prior international activity = account takeover.

cases.narrative: Finance team wired $138,000 to a vendor bank account added 48 hours prior following a spoofed CEO email requesting urgent payment. The beneficiary account was opened 6 days ago.
cases.rationale: BEC: urgency + newly-added payee + newly-opened recipient account.

cases.narrative: 12 card-not-present transactions ranging $1–$5 across different merchants in a 20-minute window — consistent with automated card testing before high-value exploitation.
cases.rationale: Automated low-value probing is a well-known fraud precursor; freeze card now.

cases.narrative: Elderly customer (82) made seven ATM cash withdrawals totalling $34,000 over 10 days following contact with an individual claiming to be a lottery official demanding taxes be paid upfront.
cases.rationale: Advance-fee elder scam; SAR category required even if customer disputes.

cases.narrative: Sudden high-value P2P transfer to a brand-new, unknown payee, deviating sharply from established spending pattern.
cases.rationale: Suspicious but a single data point — needs analyst to call the customer before acting.

cases.narrative: Monthly $400 recurring charge from a familiar streaming merchant the customer has paid for 18 consecutive months. Alert fired due to a routine category-level rule tweak.
cases.rationale: Stable recurring charge; rule-tuning noise, not fraud.

cases.narrative: Customer travelled abroad (notified the bank in advance) and used their debit card for restaurant and transport charges totalling $380 across 4 days.
cases.rationale: Travel notice on file + spending profile consistent with travel = benign.

cases.narrative: Customer bought a $2,100 laptop at a reputable electronics retailer during a Black Friday sale. Amount is above customer's rolling average but merchant category and seasonality are consistent.
cases.rationale: Large purchase alone isn't fraud; seasonality + merchant trust support clearing.

cases.narrative: Business account received a $62,000 wire from a long-standing counterparty (54 prior transfers over 3 years from same remitter). Amount is in-pattern for quarterly settlement.
cases.rationale: Established counterparty, in-pattern amount, legitimate business cadence.

cases.narrative: Single $9,500 ATM withdrawal — the only large cash activity on this account in the past year. No supporting narrative or context.
cases.rationale: Just under threshold is suspicious but one event with no corroborating signal needs human judgement.

cases.narrative: Customer added a new beneficiary 3 months ago and has sent 5 small payments ($50–$200) to it since without issue. Current flagged payment is $800 to the same beneficiary.
cases.rationale: Established payment history to this beneficiary; escalating amount but still modest.

cases.narrative: Dormant account (no activity for 14 months) suddenly initiated 6 transfers totalling $28,000 to 6 different international recipients within one evening.
cases.rationale: Dormant-account reactivation with immediate international fan-out is a strong SAR signal.
